newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar firms as March resistance eyed.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar firms as March resistance eyed.

text.p: Light buying failed to push the March white sugar contract back through the psychological $300 barrier as the London market slowly recovered from a fierce bout of selling earlier in the week, traders said on Thursday.
Commission house buying in the spot contract boosted values and the overall volume was swollen by trade May crosses and May/August spread deals, they said.
But activity was generally quiet as the market consolidated after the fireworks seen on Tuesday when March tumbled $8.00 on arbitrage sales against the raws market to hit a low of $296.70.

"There's nothing happening -- a few crosses and bits and bobs. It's really quiet, New York came off and everybody did what they needed to do," one trader said. At 1708 GMT March stood 80 cents higher at $298.50 after coming close to resistance with an intraday high of $299.80. May was up 90 cents at $298.50 and volume totalled 1,400 lots.
Market sources said this week's slide on the whites could have been excessive and a corrective bounce was expected as March's relative strength indices were hovering at the 30-value oversold barrier.

"I think you might see a run-up, maybe the whites have done a bit too much," the trader said. Paris trading was listless with just 615 lots traded. March was up $1.00 at $298.70 and May up 80 cents at $298.50.
